# Automatic Backwash Sequence: Dual-Media Gravity Filters F-1 to F-4

## 1. Scope

This sequence covers automatic backwashing of filters F-1 to F-4 using backwash pumps P-BW1/P-BW2 (duty/standby) and air scour blower B-1. It is written as a control narrative for PLC implementation. Where your brief did not specify a value, I have added an adjustable setpoint marked **[TBC]**. Section 9 lists items that must be confirmed before coding.

## 2. Equipment and Tag Convention (per filter, n = 1–4)

| Item | Tag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Influent valve | FV-n01 | Open/close |
| Effluent rate control valve | FCV-n02 | Modulating (filter flow control) |
| Backwash water valve | FCV-n03 | Modulating (backwash flow control) |
| Air scour valve | FV-n04 | Open/close |
| Drain (washwater) valve | FV-n05 | Open/close |
| Filter-to-waste valve | FV-n06 | Open/close (or modulating, see §9) |
| Headloss transmitter | PDIT-n01 | 4–20 mA |
| Effluent turbidimeter | AIT-n01 | 4–20 mA, NTU |
| Filter water level | LIT-n01 | **Required, not in brief, see §9** |

Common equipment: P-BW1/P-BW2 backwash pumps, B-1 air scour blower, clearwell level LIT-CW, backwash header flow FIT-BW (**required, see §9**).

## 3. Setpoints

| Parameter | Default | Adjustable range |
|---|---|---|
| Headloss trigger | 2.4 m | 1.5–3.0 m |
| Headloss trigger debounce | 60 s **[TBC]** | 10–300 s |
| Turbidity trigger | 0.3 NTU for 5 min | 0.1–1.0 NTU / 1–15 min |
| Max run time | 72 h | 24–120 h |
| Clearwell start permissive | ≥ 3.0 m | — |
| Clearwell low-low abort | 2.5 m **[TBC]** | — |
| Drain-down target | 0.3 m above media | 0.1–0.5 m |
| Drain-down timeout | 30 min **[TBC]** | 5–60 min |
| Air scour only | 3 min | 1–10 min |
| Air + low-rate wash | 2 min | 1–5 min |
| Low-rate wash rate | 15 m/h **[TBC]** | 5–25 m/h |
| Air scour rate | 55 m/h air **[TBC]** | per blower/media supplier |
| High-rate wash | 50 m/h for 8 min | 30–60 m/h / 4–15 min |
| High-rate ramp up / down | 60 s / 60 s **[TBC]** | 30–180 s |
| Settle | 2 min | 1–10 min |
| Filter-to-waste end | < 0.1 NTU | 0.05–0.3 NTU |
| FTW confirm time | 60 s continuous **[TBC]** | 0–300 s |
| FTW maximum | 30 min | 10–60 min |
| Min. filters online | 3 | — |
| Max filtration rate (N-1) | **[TBC], from filter area** | — |

Backwash flow is derived as **Q_BW (m³/h) = rate (m/h) × filter bed area A (m²)**. The high-rate volume per wash is 50 × A × 8/60 ≈ **6.7 × A m³**, plus the low-rate and ramp volumes. The clearwell 3.0 m permissive must be verified to hold at least this volume plus plant demand margin above the low-low level.

## 4. Initiation

### 4.1 Backwash requests (per filter, any one sets `BW_REQ_n`)

1. **Headloss:** PDIT-n01 > 2.4 m continuously for the debounce time while the filter is In Service.
2. **Turbidity:** AIT-n01 > 0.3 NTU continuously for 5 min while the filter is In Service. This trigger is **inhibited** during FTW and for 15 min **[TBC]** after return to service. It is also inhibited while AIT-n01 is faulted (bad quality, out of range, or flow alarm). A faulted turbidimeter raises an alarm and does not start a backwash.
3. **Run time:** cumulative In-Service time ≥ 72 h. The timer resets on successful return to service.
4. **Operator request:** HMI pushbutton, with confirm dialog. It is available only when the filter is In Service or Standby.

The trigger cause is latched and logged with the backwash record.

### 4.2 Queue and priority

- **Only one filter may be in backwash at a time.** A common `BW_IN_PROGRESS` interlock enforces this.
- Requests enter a FIFO queue. Priority order where several are pending at once: turbidity > headloss > operator > run time.
- A filter may only leave service if at least 3 filters will remain In Service. If plant flow ÷ 3 would exceed the maximum filtration rate, the request is held and the alarm "Backwash deferred – insufficient filter capacity" is raised.

### 4.3 Start permissives (all required at step S0)

- Clearwell LIT-CW ≥ 3.0 m
- At least one backwash pump Available (auto, healthy, no trip)
- B-1 Available
- All valves on the selected filter in Auto, with no position-fail alarms
- FIT-BW, LIT-n01 and AIT-n01 healthy
- No other filter in backwash
- Plant not in shutdown, and filter not in Maintenance/Out-of-Service mode

If a permissive is missing, the request stays queued and the HMI shows the missing permissive. An alarm is raised if the request has been held for more than 60 min **[TBC]**.

## 5. Flow Redistribution

Plant flow is 30 ML/d = 1,250 m³/h.

- 4 filters online: 312.5 m³/h each.
- 3 filters online: 416.7 m³/h each.

Each FCV-n02 controls its filter flow to **Plant flow ÷ N_online**. When a filter leaves service, the setpoints of the remaining filters ramp to the new share over 5 min **[TBC]**. This avoids rate surges that cause turbidity breakthrough. The reverse ramp applies on return to service. N_online changes at the start of S1 (leaving) and at completion of S8 (returning).

## 6. Sequence Steps

Each step has a step timeout. On timeout the sequence goes to **HOLD** with an alarm (see §7), unless stated otherwise.

| Step | Name | Actions | Transition to next step |
|---|---|---|---|
| **S0** | Request accepted | Check permissives (§4.3). Latch `BW_IN_PROGRESS`. Log start time, trigger and clearwell level. | All permissives true |
| **S1** | Isolate & drain down | Ramp other filters' rate setpoints (§5). Close influent FV-n01 (confirm closed). FCV-n02 continues filtering to the clearwell at its current setpoint, or at the max valve position if level falls slowly. | LIT-n01 ≤ media + 0.3 m. Then close FCV-n02 and confirm closed. Timeout 30 min → HOLD, alarm "Drain-down slow". The operator may select "Continue", which opens FV-n06 to finish the drain-down to waste. |
| **S2** | Air scour | Open drain FV-n05 (confirm). Open air scour FV-n04 (confirm). Start B-1, unloaded if it has a blow-off valve, then load. | B-1 running and air confirmed (run feedback, plus pressure switch if fitted) → start 3 min timer. Timer done → S3. |
| **S3** | Air + low-rate wash | Air continues. Start duty pump (P-BW1 or P-BW2 per duty selection) with FCV-n03 at minimum open. FCV-n03 then controls FIT-BW to the low-rate setpoint (rate × A). | Flow within ±10% of setpoint → start 2 min timer. **Trough protection:** if LIT-n01 reaches the "air off" level (e.g. 150 mm below the trough lip **[TBC]**) before the timer ends, end the step early and log it. This prevents media loss with air. → S4. |
| **S4** | Air off | Stop B-1. Close FV-n04 after a 5 s run-down delay **[TBC]**. Hold low-rate flow for 30 s **[TBC]** to release entrapped air. | Air valve confirmed closed and purge timer done |
| **S5** | High-rate wash | Ramp the FIT-BW setpoint from low rate to 50 m/h × A over the ramp-up time. | Flow within ±5% of setpoint → start 8 min timer (the timer runs only while flow is within band). Timer done → ramp down to zero over the ramp-down time → S6. |
| **S6** | Wash stop & settle | Close FCV-n03 (confirm). Stop the duty pump after the valve is closed. FV-n05 stays open to drain the troughs. Start 2 min settle timer. | Timer done → close FV-n05 (confirm) |
| **S7** | Refill | Open influent FV-n01. FCV-n02 and FV-n06 stay closed. The filter refills to operating level. | LIT-n01 ≥ normal operating level **[TBC]**. Timeout 20 min **[TBC]**. |
| **S8** | Filter-to-waste | Open FV-n06. Filter flow is controlled to the normal share (Plant flow ÷ 4) to waste (see §9 on how). Start the 30 min max timer. | **Normal end:** AIT-n01 < 0.1 NTU continuously for the confirm time. **Max time:** 30 min elapsed with AIT-n01 ≥ 0.1 NTU → alarm "FTW turbidity not achieved". Close FV-n06 and FV-n01. The filter goes to **Standby – Operator Release Required**; it is not returned to service automatically. |
| **S9** | Return to service | Close FV-n06 and open FCV-n02 at the same time (make-before-break, so the filter is never fully dead-headed). Ramp to the normal share. Reset the run-time counter. Activate the 15 min turbidity-trigger inhibit. | Filter In Service. Clear `BW_IN_PROGRESS`. Log end time, total wash volume, FTW duration and final turbidity. Release the next queued filter. |

### Interlocks active during the sequence

- B-1 cannot run unless FV-n04 is confirmed open on the filter in backwash.
- The BW pumps cannot run unless FCV-n03 is not closed and FV-n05 is confirmed open on the filter in backwash.
- FV-n04 and FCV-n03 cannot open while FCV-n02 or FV-n06 is open, on any filter.
- FV-n05 and FV-n01 cannot both be open at once.

## 7. Abnormal Conditions

| Condition | Response |
|---|---|
| Duty BW pump fails to start or trips | Automatically start the standby pump and keep the step and its timers running (the wash timer pauses while flow is out of band). Alarm. If both pumps fail → **ABORT**. |
| Low backwash flow (< 80% of setpoint for 30 s) during S3 or S5 | Alarm. The timer pauses. If not recovered within 2 min → HOLD. |
| B-1 fails during S2 or S3 | Alarm → HOLD. The operator may Skip Air (continue to S5) or Abort. |
| Clearwell < 2.5 m during wash | **ABORT**, alarm "Clearwell low-low". |
| Valve fails to reach position (travel time + 10 s) | HOLD, alarm naming the valve. |
| Instrument failure (FIT-BW, LIT-n01, AIT-n01) | HOLD, alarm. A failed AIT-n01 in S8 → Standby – Operator Release Required. |
| Power failure / PLC restart | The sequence does not resume automatically. All filter valves go to their fail-safe positions (to be defined, see §9). The filter is marked "Backwash incomplete". The operator must restart from S1 or manually release the filter. |

**HOLD** freezes the current outputs (pump and blower keep running at their present state, unless the cause is the equipment failure itself) and pauses timers. From HOLD the operator can choose **Resume**, **Skip Step** (only S2/S3 air, S8 FTW with supervisor permission) or **Abort**.

**ABORT** performs a safe shutdown:
1. Stop B-1 and close FV-n04.
2. Ramp down and close FCV-n03, then stop the pump.
3. Close FV-n06 and FCV-n02.
4. Leave FV-n05 open for 2 min, then close it.
5. Leave FV-n01 closed.

The filter goes to **Out of Service – Backwash Aborted**, and `BW_IN_PROGRESS` clears. The aborted filter is not re-queued automatically.

## 8. Alarms and Reporting

- **Priority alarms:** ABORT, clearwell low-low, both BW pumps failed, FTW turbidity not achieved, filter capacity deferral.
- **Warning alarms:** backwash request held over 60 min, drain-down slow, standby pump started, trough protection early end, turbidity trigger inhibited due to a faulted analyser.
- **Per-backwash log:** filter, trigger cause, start and end times, the duration of each step, wash water volume, peak headloss at start, FTW duration, final NTU, and any holds or aborts.
- **Trends:** backwashes per filter per day, and filter run length. Short runs indicate pretreatment problems.

## 9. Open Items to Confirm Before Coding

1. **Filter level transmitter.** Drain-down (S1), trough protection (S3) and refill (S7) need a water level above the media. The brief lists only a headloss transmitter. Confirm whether LIT-n01 exists, or whether the headloss instrument's high-side tapping can provide level.
2. **Backwash flow meter (FIT-BW).** It is needed to control 50 m/h and the low rate. Confirm whether flow is controlled by FCV-n03, by a pump VFD, or by a common header valve.
3. **Filter bed area A.** It sets the backwash flow, the clearwell volume check and the max filtration rate check at N-1. At 3 filters online each filter takes 416.7 m³/h, so confirm this is within the design loading.
4. **Low-rate wash rate and air scour rate.** These were not given. Obtain them from the media or underdrain supplier.
5. **FTW flow control.** Confirm whether FV-n06 is modulating, or whether FCV-n02 controls flow during FTW (that depends on where the FTW branch sits). Also confirm that AIT-n01 samples upstream of the FTW branch, so it reads the FTW water.
6. **Refill step (S7).** It is not in the brief but is required between settle and FTW. Confirm the operating level and whether a slow-start refill rate is needed.
7. **Clearwell low-low abort level** and confirmation that 3.0 m provides enough volume for one full wash.
8. **Valve fail-safe positions** on loss of air or power.
9. **FTW timeout action.** I have specified operator release rather than auto-return or auto-rewash. Confirm this matches your operating philosophy and regulatory requirements (some authorities require FTW until target turbidity regardless of time).
